title: The Last Coordination
briefing: The city faces a combined recovery deadline: utility maintenance, medical dispatch, supplier payments and resident support are competing for the same exhausted teams. A cascading outage is possible if coordination fails. Choose how to carry the accumulated civilization state through the final emergency shift.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Centralised load balancing can recover substantial capacity quickly, but it depends on a controller network that cannot be independently audited before the shift. Lifeline islands are slower and require sacrificing noncritical equipment.
private_intelligence.community: Residents want a credible recovery timetable more than another blanket promise. Community-led restoration can earn support, but different districts disagree about which services should return first.
private_intelligence.economy: Small firms can finance neighbourhood restoration if trade reopens immediately. Central stabilisation requires expensive specialist contracts; protected lifeline operations also need paid logistics while limiting normal commerce.
private_intelligence.safety: Hospitals and dispatch centres can be protected within separate utility islands. A rapid central restart or widely dispersed recovery crews leave less capacity for emergency escort and backup support during the transition.

choices.title: Stabilise from the Centre
choices.description: Concentrate specialists and resources on a rapid central restart of the utility and dispatch network.
choices.consequence: Concentrated recovery restores major technical capacity. Specialist costs weaken finances, unequal restoration erodes confidence, and reduced emergency support creates additional harm during the restart.

choices.title: Protect Lifeline Islands
choices.description: Ring-fence hospital, water and dispatch lifelines, publish a staged plan, and accept managed loss of noncritical equipment.
choices.consequence: Protected lifelines reduce immediate harm and the staged plan earns confidence. Sacrificed equipment lowers infrastructure capacity, and restricted commerce plus logistics costs weaken the economy.

choices.title: Release Neighbourhood Recovery
choices.description: Reopen local trade and let funded community teams restore services in parallel, with central crews reserved for advice.
choices.consequence: Local trade and participation rebuild economic capacity and trust. Dispersed restoration overloads technical coordination, while gaps in emergency support increase harm.
